name: Jehn's random-basket coin game: exact optimal expected win for 2 baskets beyond n = 22 (OEIS A391791) and 3 baskets beyond n = 18 (A391792)
compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (exact backward induction over (remaining-coin set, basket-sum profile) states, layer by layer; memory, not time, is the limit: roughly 2^n * T/2 states for 2 baskets, T = n(n+1)/2, so the largest two adjacent layers reach about 1.5e10 entries near n = 26; rough estimates, not measured)
statement: Coins worth 1, 2, ..., n are placed one per turn for n turns. Each turn one of k baskets is chosen uniformly at random and the player then puts one remaining coin of their choice into it; after the last turn the player takes the basket with the largest sum. A391791 (k = 2) gives a(n) = 2^(n-1) times the maximum expected win; A391792 (k = 3) gives 3^(n-1) times it. Both are by Ruediger Jehn (the author of the 'Risk or Safety' sequences A387261/A387262), carry keywords nonn,hard,more, and have not been extended since they were added (Dec 20 2025 and Dec 31 2025; last edits Jan 07 2026). Known terms: A391791 for n = 1..22 (1, 5, 20, 65, 190, 530, 1407, 3585, 8942, 21819, 52204, 123190, 287044, 661329, 1509949, 3420580, 7688444, 17173896, 38143782, 84262365, 185278522, 405700861); A391792 for n = 1..18 (1, 7, 40, 192, 837, 3423, 13478, 51396, 190809, 693595, 2477822, 8740848, 30419671, 104752091, 357748926, 1211285880, 4074000387, 13615817865). A391791 also states a conjecture: for n > 9 the optimal first move is to put coin floor((n+3)/2) in the first basket. Jehn's program is a Julia file linked from A391791 (a391791_1.jl.txt). OPEN as of 2026-10-14: no term beyond n = 22 (k = 2) or n = 18 (k = 3) in the entries. The earlier page review could not retrieve the OEIS sources (HTTP 403), so the sequence frontiers remain input-reported.
success_criterion: CONFIRMED: the exact integer values of A391791(23), A391791(24), A391791(25) AND A391792(19), A391792(20), A391792(21) (K = 3 new terms of each; direction: new terms), under the entries' own definitions (a(n) = k^(n-1) times the maximum, over all adaptive placement strategies, of the expected largest basket sum; baskets chosen independently and uniformly each turn; coins 1..n each used exactly once), each computed by two independently written exact programs that (i) agree on every new term, (ii) reproduce every published term (A391791 n = 1..22, A391792 n = 1..18), and (iii) use integer or rational arithmetic only (no floating point anywhere in the value recursion). The terms must not already be in the OEIS entries, their b-files or their edit history at verification time. Submitting to the OEIS is an action for the human only.

partial_wins.statement: The three new terms of only one of the two sequences (A391791 n = 23..25, or A391792 n = 19..21), with the same two-program confirmation and calibration.

A settled status for A391791's stated conjecture over a range: for every n from 10 through the largest n computed, the full set of optimal first moves listed exactly, either confirming that coin floor((n+3)/2) is optimal for each n or giving the first n where it is not (a counterexample to the conjecture as stated in the entry).

verification_method: Write the recursion from the definition: V(R, s) = (1/k) * sum over baskets b of max over coins c in R of V(R - {c}, s + c*e_b), with V(empty, s) = max(s); canonicalise s by sorting (baskets are exchangeable) and, for k = 2, use only the difference |s1 - s2| because the total placed is fixed by R. For a state with m = |R| turns remaining, store W(R,s) = k^m V(R,s), so W(empty,s) = max(s) and W(R,s) = sum_b max_c W(R-{c},s+c*e_b) are exact integers. At the empty-basket initial state, the published term is W(R,0)/k because the first random basket is irrelevant by symmetry; verify divisibility by k. Use arbitrary-precision integers or prove fixed-width safety for every intermediate value. Sweep layers by |R| from 0 up to n, keeping two layers in memory. Calibrate on every published term, then compute the new terms with a second, independently written program (different language or different state encoding, e.g. full sorted sum vector instead of differences) and require exact agreement. Optionally publish per-layer SHA-256 hashes of the value tables so a third checker can compare layer by layer.
status_checked: 2026-10-14; historical proposal date preserved. No fresh source request was made during final preparation. The earlier page review could not retrieve the OEIS sources (HTTP 403), so the sequence frontiers remain input-reported.
angles: Two baskets: the state is (remaining set R, |s1 - s2|); the difference has the parity of the placed total, which halves the table; store layer |R| = m as C(n, m) rows indexed by subset rank.
Three baskets: state (R, sorted (s1, s2, s3)); the number of sorted triples for placed total P is about P^2/12, so n = 19..21 is far smaller than it looks.
Evaluator first: reproduce n <= 12 in seconds with a memoised recursion, then switch to the layered sweep and confirm it matches before scaling.
Parallelise inside a layer: each subset R's row depends only on the next layer, so cores split subsets with no locking.
pitfalls: The basket is chosen BEFORE the player picks the coin each turn; reversing the order changes the game (the adversarial siblings A391537/A391538 are different sequences).
The player takes the larger basket at the end (max), not a fixed basket.
a(n) is scaled by k^(n-1), not k^n: the first coin's basket choice does not matter by symmetry. Check the scaling against a(3) = 20 (k = 2) and a(3) = 40 (k = 3).
Do not search only strategies of the conjectured form; the maximum is over all adaptive strategies.
Memory grows as 2^n times the sum range: estimate the largest layer before launching, and do not trust this entry's size estimates without measuring.
